children: Gold could trade around $5,000 to $5,500 next year, Ole Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo said at a media briefing. In the longer term, gold could rise even higher as central banks haven't finished accumulating the precious metal, which will take some time, he says. A key support level this year is $4,000, which may not hold if there is an escalation in energy prices and the inflationary outlook, Hansen said. If prices don't fall below $4,000, gold could approach $4,500 by year-end, he added. "I think gold should still be considered as a store of value, so one that beats inflation in the long run, and one that's good to have on a rainy day where something could potentially go wrong elsewhere," Hansen said. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)
